quiz.q: You need to fetch one specific employee by a value that uniquely identifies them. How should that value be passed?
quiz.explain: URI parameters are part of the path and identify a unique, mandatory resource. A name isn't unique — 10 people may be called Mahesh.

quiz.q: A request asks for all employees who have left: `GET /employees?status=inactive`. Why is `status` a query parameter rather than a URI parameter?
options: It can match 0, 5 or 20 employees — it filters a collection and is optional
Status must always be in the body
quiz.explain: A URI parameter narrows to exactly one unique resource; status filters a collection, so it's a query parameter.

quiz.q: Which expression reads the URI parameter `empId` from `/employees/{empId}`?
quiz.explain: URI params arrive in attributes; the key is `uriParams` (lower-case u, upper-case P) and must match the path name exactly.

quiz.q: What does `attributes.queryParams` return when no key is given?
options: All query parameters as key–value pairs
quiz.explain: Without a key, `attributes.queryParams` (or `attributes.uriParams`) returns all of them.

quiz.q: Which three purposes are query parameters used for?
quiz.explain: The slide: query params filter, sort and paginate the collection of a result.
offset = records to skip; page n with limit L has offset (n−1)×L, so page 3 → 200.

quiz.q: How is the page size for pagination usually decided?
options: It is fixed at 100 by HTTP
By the number of query parameters in RAML
quiz.explain: E.g. 25 records may load in 75 ms while a larger page is too slow for customers.

quiz.q: RAML declares 5 query parameters and a client sends 125. What happens by default?
quiz.explain: Rejecting them automatically is a myth; you must enable query parameters strict validation in the APIkit Router.

quiz.q: Where do you enable rejection of undeclared query parameters and headers?
options: APIkit Router configuration: Query parameters / Headers Strict Validations
quiz.explain: With strict validation on, only parameters/headers declared in the spec are allowed; others get 400 Bad Request.

quiz.q: How do you make a RAML type reject fields in the request body that aren't defined?
options: Nothing — extra fields are rejected by default
quiz.explain: `additionalProperties` defaults to true, so extra fields are accepted unless set to false.

quiz.q: An insider with valid credentials sends 5 lakh characters in one query parameter. What prevents the crash?
options: Length restrictions such as `minLength`/`maxLength` in the spec
quiz.explain: Security passes because the credentials are valid; validation of lengths rejects oversized input before processing.

quiz.q: Why is strict validation not needed for URI parameters?
options: They are part of the fixed path — extra ones can't be added without changing the path
quiz.explain: The path either matches the defined resource or not.

cards.back: Also called a **path parameter**. Part of the path that uniquely identifies a resource, e.g. `/employees/101`. Mandatory.
`?key=value&key2=value2` after the path; optional; used to **filter, sort, paginate**.

cards.front: URI vs. query parameter — the rule
cards.back: Mandatory value that identifies a unique resource → URI param. Optional filter/sort/paginate value → query param.
`attributes.uriParams.<name>` and `attributes.queryParams.<name>`. Without a key, you get all of them.
`/departments/{deptId}/employees/{empId}` → `attributes.uriParams.deptId`, `attributes.uriParams.empId`.
`GET /employees?status=inactive` → `SELECT * FROM employees WHERE status = :status`.
`GET /employees?status=active&orderBySalary=asc` (or `desc`).
Returning results in consecutive chunks (pages) so a UI doesn't load thousands of records at once.
`limit` = records per page; `offset` = records to skip. Page n → offset (n−1)×limit.
Through discussion and performance testing, not randomly.

cards.front: Extra query params beyond the RAML — rejected by default?
cards.back: No. By default they're accepted. Enable **Query parameters Strict Validations** in the APIkit Router.
APIkit Router option that rejects headers not declared in the API spec (400 Bad Request).
Component generated from the RAML that routes and validates requests; its config holds the strict-validation options.
RAML type option controlling undeclared body fields. Default **true** (accepted); set **false** to reject them.
String length restrictions in RAML; e.g. `transaction-id` with both = 20 accepts exactly 20 characters.
Restricts a value to a fixed list, e.g. `origin` accepts only `mobile` or `webApp`.

cards.front: Why validate if the API is secured?
cards.back: A caller with valid credentials can still send huge values that crash the app; validation rejects them first.

cards.front: When is strict validation most important?
cards.back: When the API has external/third-party consumers or is exposed to the internet (e.g. a bank's API used by NBFCs).

cards.front: Where are body vs. header/query restrictions set?
cards.back: Body: in RAML (`additionalProperties`, lengths). Headers and query params strictness: in the APIkit Router.
Listener **exposes** your API; Request **calls** another API (consuming a third-party service).
